title: Hill climbing that learns from lost rounds: mirror and credit
question: Does hill climbing find more improvements when it learns from the rounds it loses: trying the opposite direction after a clear loss (mirror), and choosing which knobs to nudge from a per-knob model of all past rounds (credit)?
change: --mirror: after a round lost by at least 1 point, the next round tests the same knob moves in the opposite direction. --credit: a per-knob linear model of the margin, fitted on every round and weighted by games, picks knobs and directions by Thompson sampling; 25% of rounds stay random; the evidence is halved after each keep. Both off by default.
method: Tuning run (hill climbing), 100,000 games, against a control run of the same budget and seed
measured: Tuning run, 100,000 games, vs a control
